summary: Added a deterministic, stdlib-only production-readiness scaffold that distinguishes the existing deterministic local vector skeleton (is_real_embedding_model=false, in-process) from a real production setup. build_embedding_provider_readiness / validate_embedding_provider_config classify a provider config, requiring a real provider name + model + positive dim + credential_source (an env var NAME, never a secret value) and rejecting credential-shaped fields. build_vector_store_plan / validate_vector_store_plan mark in-memory/process-local stores as NOT production-ready and require a known persistent backend. build_vector_index_readiness aggregates provider+store+index into a production_ready verdict that is true only for a complete DECLARED config, and always reports current_shipped_state.production_ready=false. A CLI tools/check_vector_production_readiness.py exits nonzero on the repo default. No provider call, no store install, no network, no credential/.env read; the original ROADMAP item stays unchecked with a checked sub-note for the scaffold.

roadmap_item_status: UNCHECKED — 'real embedding provider + persistent vector store + production index' is NOT marked done; only the deterministic local skeleton exists. A checked sub-note for the gated readiness scaffold was added.
risks: production_ready=true is a CONFIG-COMPLETENESS verdict, not a connectivity/authentication/benchmark check; a fully-declared but wrong config would read as ready. It gates human intent, it does not validate a live provider.
The persistent-store allow-list is a fixed set of known backends; a valid but unlisted store is warned (not accepted) and would need the list updated.
The scaffold reads only declared metadata; it deliberately never resolves credential_source to an actual secret, so it cannot confirm a credential is present or valid.
Wiring a real provider later must register it in VECTOR_EMBEDDER_FACTORIES and only then read config/credentials — this scaffold intentionally does not open that path.

Environment note: the local interpreter is python3 (no bare 'python' on PATH); the quality-gate runner honors PYTHON=python3, and a local 'python->python3' PATH shim lets its default-interpreter meta-test pass.
credentials: No credentials or .env files were read, created, or modified; provider/store validators reject credential-shaped value fields and the scaffold uses only a credential_source env-var NAME.
No external network calls, provider calls, or vector-DB installs were used for implementation or local tests.
